newsitem.title: USA: Louisiana legislature adopts $12.6 billion budget.
newsitem.headline: Louisiana legislature adopts $12.6 billion budget.

text.p: The Louisiana legislature has approved a $12.6 billion budget that boosts education spending without renewing a sales tax, The Advocate reported Monday.
The House unanimously approved the budget Sunday night, adopting changes made previously in the Senate. The legislature is scheduled to adjourn Monday evening.
Gov. Mike Foster had sought renewal of the one-cent sales tax on food, which raises $110 million a year, to increase education spending.

The final version of the budget allows the tax to expire on June 30. It uses $360 million of surplus revenues to retire general obligation early over the next four years, freeing up money that otherwise would go to debt service to pay for teacher pay raises.
The debt defeasement was approved last week by the Louisiana Bond Commission.

The budget allocates $65.2 million for pay raises of at least $1,000 each for public school teachers. It allocates $166.1 million for salary increases for non-teaching staff at public schools, $38.2 million for classroom computers, $30 million for reading and math programs in the lower grades, and $11.4 million for teaching supplies.
The budget allocates $3.28 billion for the state's Medicaid program, which faces $91 million in spending cuts.

It uses $19.4 million from the Mineral Revenue and Settelement Fund to pay off state pension system debt, and gives the Louisiana State University Medical Center $43.5 million to replace reserve funds used for operations in previous years.
The budget does not allocate any money for the state's proposed rainy day fund, which still must be approved by voters in the form of a constitutional amendment.
The budget now goes to Foster, who has a line-item veto.
